turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_supercon_train.csv: 300 real materials, columns `composition`
    (element fractions as a compact formula string) and `target` (the
    measured critical temperature Tc (K)).
  - b3_supercon_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE materials whose critical temperature
    Tc (K) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and `composition`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST critical
temperature Tc (K), then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training data show a clear hierarchy: the highest Tc values are all layered cuprates, with the very top belonging to Hg/Tl/Bi–Ba/Sr–Ca–Cu–O families (HgBa₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈₊δ ≈ 118–137 K, TlBa₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈ ≈ 108–123 K, Bi/Pb–Sr–Ca–Cu–O ≈ 91–111 K). Non‑cuprates (borocarbides, pnictides, A15, elemental) are all far lower. So I rank pool candidates by proximity to these top cuprate families, favoring Hg‑ and Tl‑based multi‑Cu‑layer compositions, then Pb‑doped Bi‑Sr‑Ca‑Cu‑O.

- c084 Hg₀.₇Bi₀.₃Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O₈.₃₅ — Hg‑based 3‑Cu‑layer cuprate, closest analog to the 118–137 K Hg‑1223/1234 records.
- c034 Tl₂Ba₂Ca₅Cu₆O₁₆ — Tl‑Ba‑Ca‑Cu‑O multi‑layer, same family as Tl‑1223/1234 (108–123 K).
- c097 Bi₁.₆Pb₀.₄Sr₂Ca₃Cu₄Ag₀.₀₀₄O — Pb‑doped Bi‑Sr‑Ca‑Cu‑O ~4 Cu layers, near Bi1.6Pb0.3Te0.1Sr2Ca3Cu4O (102.7 K).
- c046 Bi₁.₇Pb₀.₂Mo₀.₁Sr₂Ca₂Cu₃O — close to Bi1.7Pb0.3Sr2Ca2Cu3O (106.2 K).
- c081 Bi₃.₂Pb₀.₂V₀.₆Sr₄Ca₅Cu₇O — high‑Cu‑count Bi/Pb‑Sr‑Ca‑Cu‑O, Bi‑2223‑like scaled up.

Final: c084, c034, c097, c046, c081
